problems.title: Leaf-first SCOUT incurs a cost excluded by its finite bound
problems.source_location: Algorithm 4 and Theorem 5.2, arXiv v3 PDF p.7; Appendix A.3
claim: The theorem bounds full-window SCOUT leaf inspections by \(\sum_{s=-n+1}^n I_{\rm test}^{x,s}(h)\), but the proof assumes empty windows cost zero even at a leaf.
analysis: Take \(n=1,b=2,h=2\), root value \(0\), ordinary-child distribution concentrated at \(0\); the entire legal negamax tree is zero. TEST at thresholds \(0,1\) costs \(2,2\), total \(4\). Printed SCOUT first pays two reads testing the first child, then one read in its improving re-search, then rereads that leaf at window \([0,0]\), and finally tests the other root child once: total \(5>4\). Every game value returned is correct. A full-support uniform distribution on \(\{-1,0,1\}\), conditional root \(0\), likewise gives expected SCOUT \(11/2\) versus summed TEST \(115/24\); the point-mass case is not essential.
result: The exact finite-cost bound does not describe the printed guard order. This does not establish wrong game values or falsify the asymptotic comparison.
repair: Check the empty window before reading a leaf to match the proof. Alternatively, for nonempty full windows \(n\ge1\), every extra read can be charged to a preceding TEST read, giving printed cost at most twice corrected cost. That fixed factor preserves the asymptotic upper growth bound when limits exist; it does not restore the finite prefactor one.
